name: Quality control

subjectOf.text: Human shortcomings in micro task work such as limited attention span, irrationality, and inaccuracy create a need for verification, but manual verification fails as a remedy because the verifiers are subject to the same human limitations.
subjectOf.abstract: All too human shortcomings of micro task works, such as limited attention span, irrationality, and inaccuracies result in verification requirements for micro task work. However, manual verification of micro task work is subject to the same human limitations.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900
scope_conditions: manual verification of micro task work

subjectOf.text: To offset human limitations, requesters in centralized micro task structures assign the same task to teams of up to fifteen workers to form a consensus.
subjectOf.abstract: In an attempt to ensure quality of results and minimize the impact of the human limitations of their workers, requesters in centralized micro task structures set up teams of up to 15 workers to perform the same task in an effort to form a consensus.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900

subjectOf.text: Consensus by redundancy fails economically: multiplying the same work across many workers significantly increases the cost of micro task work.
subjectOf.abstract: The multiplication of work inherent in this process significantly increases the cost of micro task work.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900
scope_conditions: centralized platforms using redundant task assignment

subjectOf.text: Rather than repeating the same task across many workers to reach quality, the architecture verifies quality directly by examining and validating individual worker task performance through reputation verification.
subjectOf.abstract: Instead of repeating work on given tasks to attain high quality work products for micro tasks, Semada uses an architecture of reputation verification that examines micro worker task performance and verifies the validity and quality of the work.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900
scope_conditions: micro tasks routed through the reputation verification architecture

subjectOf.text: Because requesters select workers by reputation score, workers acquire an incentive to keep their scores high by performing tasks with high accuracy and efficiency.
subjectOf.abstract: Requesters can select workers based on their reputation score, giving workers an incentive to keep the reputation scores high by performing micro tasks with high accuracy and efficiency.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900
scope_conditions: requesters can observe and select on reputation score

subjectOf.text: Centralized platforms cannot simply drop identity verification, because they need it to keep malicious actors from abusing the network and to ensure work quality; this is the tradeoff a staking based design is meant to dissolve.
subjectOf.abstract: However, centralized micro task platforms need to verify identity to prevent malicious actors from abusing the network and ensure work quality.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900

subjectOf.text: Human shortcomings in micro task work such as limited attention span, irrationality, and inaccuracy create verification requirements, but manual verification is performed by humans subject to the same limitations, so verification does not resolve the quality problem it is meant to solve.
subjectOf.abstract: However, manual verification of micro task work is subject to the same human limitations.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, AI Learning - Decentralized Governance to Optimize Human Output Datasets for AI Learning (2024). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4755632
scope_conditions: applies where verification of micro task work is itself manual

subjectOf.text: Gamification supplies quality control by making workers review and rate each other's contributions for points or recognition, which surfaces and resolves discrepancies through consensus-based voting or peer review rather than through duplicated independent work.
subjectOf.abstract: Gamification can be utilized to improve data quality through mechanisms like consensus-based voting or peer review. Workers can review and rate each other's contributions, earning points or recognition for accurate and consistent work.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, AI Learning - Decentralized Governance to Optimize Human Output Datasets for AI Learning (2024). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4755632

subjectOf.text: Maintaining consistent annotation quality across many annotators and automated systems is unsolved at scale, and small labeling errors translate into significant degradation of model performance in critical applications.
subjectOf.abstract: With the scale at which data annotation occurs, maintaining consistent quality across different annotators or automated systems remains a practical challenge. Small errors in annotation can have significant impacts on model performance
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Artificial Intelligence The Final Frontier (2025). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5095633
scope_conditions: safety-critical applications such as autonomous driving

subjectOf.text: Validation Pools are stipulated as mechanisms in which members stake non transferable reputation tokens to vote on the approval or disapproval of transactions, proposals, or activities, and this staking mechanism carries the paper's decentralized quality control function.
subjectOf.abstract: Validation Pools are mechanisms in which members stake their reputation tokens to vote on the approval or disapproval of transactions, proposals, or activities.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, How can we Best Monitor AI Agents (2025). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5245185
scope_conditions: web3 governance with non transferable reputation tokens
